sections.content: As an introductory course, it will provide adequate and appropriate contents for a new programmer. This course is based on Python, which is thought to be easier than Java or C++. For myself, it is very friendly and easy to learn. All the contents in midterm and final will be covered in lectures(if you don't skip them). By the way, never try to skip any lab works regardless of whether you need to submit it. It's an essential way to finish a program (at least a part of it) by yourself.
sections.teaching: Gibson LAM is a very perfect instructor in this term. He will demostrate all the commands shown in the ppt(unless it's too simple). I think his English is easy and comfortable to follow and his lectures were not boring at all.  And TA Jimmy Wong was also very kind and answer our questions about almost everything.
sections.grading:
Lab works make up approximately half of the grade. But it is easy to get full marks as you can test your program before submission. (Do test it several times or you may find that you get a 0 grade if the main program crashed)

Midterm won't be calculated in the total grade if you haven't perform well and it will make your grade lower, i.e. your grade will depend on lab and final only in this case.

I have heard that the exams were quite easy in previous semesters, but it's absolutey not that case in 20-21 fall term. In fact, we received an gentle email after final by David Rossiter which said "I don't think you need me to tell you that it's a very hard exam!".  But for me, I admit it's a little hard and time was not enough to answer all the questions, but it never beyond the workload. Well, not so bad.

My grade: A+
Lab: 3 *100/100 for three submissions in total
Midterm: 87.5/100  (Mean: 64)
Final:91.45/100 (Mean: 55)
[for reference only]
sections.workload:
I think the workload is fine and appropriate. We have discussed basic commands, turtle graphics, data structure, functions and objects, file input and output(a little hard and not covered in the final).

Basically, lab works(once a week) will help you remember most of commands discussed in the lectures. But you will also need to review lecture notes for preparing exams. I hadn't done extra exercises beyond those provided by the course. Maybe I should do so.

sections.content:
Python programming
Turtle graphics is used as a teaching aid to visualize the code.
Textbook: Interactive Python Programming
for Beginners written by Gibson Lam and David Rossiter
Content:
0. basic python commands: print(), input(),
1. turtle commands: turtle.color , turtle.forward(), turtle.backward(), turtle.goto(,)......
2. list, tuples, dictionaries
3. for loops, while loops, nested loops
4. if statements, operators
5. handling events: drag events, click events
6. file handling
7. slicing
8. Object-oriented programming
9. recursion
10. functions
11. timers
sections.teaching:
Professor Lam was a good teacher. Aside from the examples provided in the course notes, Prof. Lam gave extra examples he created by himself to demonstrate the concepts explicitly so that beginners could understand the idea of programming and the functions of the commands.
The TA, Jimmy was helpful. He replied to students' questions in lessons immediately and gave students additional knowledge to satisfy their curiosity.
sections.grading:
Two ways in calculating the final grade.
1.Midterm 24%, Lab projects 36%, Final exam 40%
2.Midterm 0%, Lab projects 42%, Final exam 58%
The highest mark of these two calculations will be automatically chosen.
The final exam was difficult because the higher-ups of HKUST pressured the course to do harder exam.
I suggest beginners to practice coding daily(try playing with the code examples provided in the course notes  e.g. inserting commands, deleting commands, try doing some python coding online test on various websites etc. ) if they want to attain A range. They should also do more past papers, which will be provided by the professors before the midterm exam and the final exam.
sections.workload:

The labs were challenging . As a beginner , the labs required much more efforts and time to finish.

sections.grading:
[INCLUDED]
Labs are very manageable:
they do take some time, but the course-web guides you through it, so you shouldn't have too many problems getting full marks on them. There is a marking scheme for every lab, so make sure you double-check your code every time before you submit it.

The midterm was relatively easy and short:
Make sure that you familiarize yourself with the concepts taught, so you don't run into any time problems during the exam.

The final exam was in comparison much more difficult:
Same as the midterm: MAKE SURE that you familiarize yourself with the concepts taught, so you don't run into any time problems during the exam.
To solve some of the questions of the second part of the exam, some "out of the box"-thinking is required. Prepare for that by writing your own code snippets when revising, fiddling around with the code, and trying to solve similar problems through different approaches.

[NOT INCLUDED]
There is no ATTENDANCE:
For people who have some sort of coding experience, most of the time, it is absolutely sufficient to look over the PPTs only. But let me stress it again, don't underestimate the final exam!
sections.workload:
The workload consists ONLY of the labs:
There are only 5 labs, which you have to hand in, but also finish the other labs, just to make sure you know what's up ;)

good luck :)

sections.content:
I had taken DSE ICT before, so I understood the logic of programming pretty easily. This course taught you the basics of Python, which is a beginner-friendly programming language. The hardest part for me to understand would be the dictionary and recursion part, but this would be in the last part of the course.

I did go through all the given past papers. But since the exam changed to be online, it was much different and in some way more difficult as well. Although you are allowed to use Python, you won't have enough time to think.
sections.teaching: Gibson is a funny and friendly professor. He would stay behind the lectures to answer questions. TA Jimmy is nice too, he would answer questions clearly during the lecture.
sections.grading: The grading mainly consists of the midterm, labs, and final exam. They have 2 calculating methods and they would choose the best marks out of the 2 so you won't need to worry about that. The labs are easy to get full marks by following every instruction. I did ok for the midterm, but I didn't do very well for the canvas exam. But, I think the grade is lenient. I only got 1 question correct for part A of the final, which is 40% of the exam. I still got B+.
sections.workload: It is light. You have labs every week, but only 3 of them are graded. All you have to do is to watch videos and follow what Jimmy said. Every code is given to you except for the last 2 labs.

Most of the content taught in the lectures aren't like hard to understand (like pretty much all of them except maybe recursion), there's detailed instructions for labs too, so even if you are a beginner you should be able to handle them just fine if you try.

Content (I don't bother spending much time on this one part, literally most other reviews has it but eh here you go) :
-Turtle Graphics
-Comments, Variables and Text, Variable Types and Operators
-If condition; for ,while loop
-Lists(Array), Tuples and Strings
-Functions
-Turtle Window Event Handling
-File Handling
-Programming with Objects
-Recursion

And some other stuff but eh that about sums up the main things

sections.grading:
2 formulas for grading, where they will take the highest mark that they get from one of the formulas as your overall grade.

1. 24% Midterm, 36% Labs, 40% Finals
2. 0% Midterm, 42% Labs, 58% Finals

From what I've read there used to be bonus grade given (?) but we don't have that this sem.

As you can see, if you are able to score well in the finals, even if you messed up in midterm you can still clutch back and get a good grade.

From what I've observed A range should be around above mean + 1 standard deviation
(What the mean and the standard deviation are would be announced in email after they have finished marking the midterm/final)

For lab most people get full marks for all of them so (mid term and) final is pretty much what decides your grade.

I know I just said mid term grade technically can be excluded but I have to say mid term is definitely easier than finals. Unless you have prior knowledge on programming and you are confident that you will do good in the exam I highly recommend you to take the mid term seriously and try not to mess up.

The finals in recent years are harder because they have been pressured to make the finals harder.

-Full mark for all the labs
-Mid term:88.92% {mean:64.4%,standard deviation:21.5%}
-Final:95.71% {mean:55.9%,standard deviation:20.5%}

Final letter grade: A+

The stuff before Mid-Term is easy. Just very simple logic of programming. After Mid-Term it turns harder and takes time to understand. I advise you to study your exams earlier if you decided to skip all lectures.
sections.teaching:
Prof. Rossiter's Teaching is great. He uses different examples in the class and not only reading out all the powerpoints. He also has interactive questions or polling to check whether students could understand the underlying principles. However, in my personal view, if you got some programming background (programming courses or experience before entering university), you could just skip the lectures. I don't think it is necessary to attend lectures, and there is also no attendance too. You could simply understand the concepts by studying powerpoints and go over the examples provided.

Lab sessions are not compulsory, only go to the sessions when you encounter problems.
sections.grading:

Mid-Term: 24%
Final: 40%

I got full mark in labs, almost full mark in Mid-Term and +1.32 SD in Final. Got an A. Fair Grading tho I thought I could get an A+.

sections.content:
You're introduced to Python by the turtle module. Everything before midterm is fairly easy. Things involved include (but not limited to):
If/Elif/Else
For/While loops
Strings/Lists
random module

Post-midterm content gets difficult really quickly. I suggest spending more time on recursion because it's kind of a difficult concept to wrap your head around. You'll definitely want to study hard if you want good grades.
sections.teaching:
Cecia Chan is kind of like your average teacher. Nothing special, but she does try to make the lesson sound more interesting, and she goes through examples clearly.
Gibson Lam is lively and provides very interesting examples during lectures. You'll probably be entertained by his lectures. I've only watched two videos of his lectures and found them very useful.

Lessons involve quite a bit of demonstrations, so it's not overrun by powerpoint-reading like some other courses. Their English is fluent and can be understood easily. Overall, my experience with this course's lectures are positive and I think they're of a high quality.
sections.grading:
They have two grading methods (best one will be chosen):
Labs 36%, Midterm 24%, Final 40% or
Labs 42%, Midterm 0%, Final 58%

Scoring full on labs aren't really difficult, just make sure you be very careful and test more possible cases. Lab averages are really high though because a lot of people score full.

The midterm exam wasn't difficult in my opinion, and this seems to match what other people think. It might not be as easy if you don't have any programming experience, but I don't think it's very harsh on beginners.

The final exam was hellish. Rossiter did say that they were pressured to do harder final exams (understandable, since we have access to Python, which makes everything easier), so past papers didn't really reflect the difficulty of the exam. There was an error with one of the questions and they gave us marks for that, which helped a bit.

Here's a bit of statistics from this semester's exams:
Midterm: Avg 64.4%, SD 21.5%
Final: Avg 55.9%, SD 20.5%
*weakest question in each part of midterm/final were removed iirc

Grades for reference:
Lab 100%
Midterm ~90%
Final ~60%
Letter Grade: A-
sections.workload:
Personally I found the workload acceptable.
The lectures and (online) labs aren't compulsory and you can go to whichever session you please, so it makes managing your schedule easier.
I managed to finish all 3 hand-in lab projects and scored full without attending a lab session. It takes quite a bit of time, but the instructions given on the website are more than enough for you to complete it.
There are other labs and you're encouraged to go through them yourself, but you could skip them if you really don't have time. the only annoying part about labs is that **the hand-in date depends on your lab day while the materials are released on the same day for everyone. That means people who have assigned lab sessions on Friday essentially have a few more days to work on their programs than those assigned to Monday sessions. Definitely start early because:
1) It's not something you want to deadline-rush
2) You should try to secure 100% in all labs because most people do

sections.workload:
Light workload.

There are 7 labs in total and only 3 are hand-in labs. It took around 3-4 hours or less each for all 7 labs. I have a little programming background (learned C, C++ and Java before Uni) so it might take a few more hours if you are a complete beginner. But all instructions are given for each lab. So if you just carefully follow the instructions, it is quite straightforward.

Midterm is much much much much much easier than finals so do make sure that you take the midterm seriously. It will help a lot for your grades.

Some questions in final demand you to make a program to get to the answer. Even if they don't, knowing how to make a simple program to find the answer helps a lot. So try to get familiar with programming in Python so that you know what and how to code in different occasions.

It's about understanding than memorizing. All course materials and even the internet are accessible during both final and midterm but they are not so useful due to limited time, so try to memorize all functions and grammar.

sections.grading:
The course uses 2 grading schemes: 36% lab assignments, 23% midterms and 41% finals OR 44% lab assignments and 56% finals.

DO NOT take the midterm in a relaxed manner just because "it doesn't count even if I mess up". The midterm is extremely easy compared to the finals. The mean of the midterms is closer to about 80 whereas the mean of the finals was actually closer to 40. So even if you are well above the mean in the finals, you may fail to get A range since most people will be scoring a higher raw mark in the midterms.

I got 89 in midterms and about 60 in finals and ended up with an A.

sections.content:
Basic python programming:
1. Getting started with Python
2. Beginning to program Python (Input and Output)
3. Introduction to turtle graphics
4. Making decisions (if-elif-else structure, nested if statements)
5. Loops (while loops)
6. Using loops with turtle graphics
7. Using for loops
8. Using for loops with turtle graphics
9. Lists and tuples
10. Handling repeating patterns (using modulus)
11. More on loops (continue, break)
12. Slicing
13. Handling of data types
14. More on lists and strings
15. Functions
16. Turtle shapes
17. Creating turtles
18. Clicking and dragging turtles
19. Handling key presses
20. Clicking on the turtle window
21. More on functions
22. More on operators
23. Using Timers
24. Dictionaries
25. File handling
26. Recursion
sections.teaching:
Teaching is great as David is very passionate in the lectures as he often exceeds the lecture time of 50 minutes. He is very logical throughout the lectures and provide a lot of examples to help understanding.

The TA Jimmy is also very helpful. He has been giving timely feedbacks on labs, grades, and updates on the course website. Videos and detailed instructions are very helpful to finish the labs.
sections.grading:
There are two grading schemes, and the higher one is automatically chosen.
1. 3*12% labs + 23% Mid-term + 41% Final
2. 3*14% labs + 0% Mid-term + 58% Final (weird numbers)

I am not exactly sure the percentage of each letter grade, so I cannot make a very decent comment in the section. The following numbers are for your reference:

1. First hand-in lab: Mean = 97.5, SD = 10.5, Max = 100
2. Second hand-in lab: Mean = 96.2, SD = 9.1, Max = 100
3. Third hand-in lab: Mean = 95.7, SD = 9.7, Max = 100
4. Mid-term: Mean = 75.2, SD = 15.2, Max = 100
5. Final: Mean = 41.1, SD = 13.8, Max = 81.4
sections.workload:
The workload is not quite heavy to be honest. There are six labs in total but only three are hand-in labs for submission. So just take some time to finish the labs, they are by no means hard. And in fact, the mean for every lab is crazily high. The TAs will also help you finish the labs, and there are very detailed instructions on the website.

Also, the exams are open-book, and they do not require memorising a lot. Understanding the content is more than enough to deal with the exams. But the final this semester is super hard :(

sections.content: The content is about the basic knowledge of python, which is a very nice introduction course for those who haven't get in touch with coding before.
sections.teaching:
David is so experienced at teaching in several aspects:

1. As a British, he's certainly aware of the English level of the students may not be very high, and in the lectures, he controls the range of words he used carefully and also repeat and stress whenever it comes to the key point.

2. He's quite familiar with where the beginners might feel confused and would explain thoroughly in class.

3. The topic of examples relate closely to the social focus, and it works effectively in waking us up at 9
:00 in the morning

As for the TA Jimmy:

Jimmy is so nice! Best TA in the world!
As we have full-online teaching this semester, I can only tell about the advantages I feel in this mode of teaching.Whenever you come across problem in class, Jimmy is always waiting in the zoom chat box to answer. (Always precise and clear, and you can take a screenshot to save those answers in case forget.) At this level I really appreciate the online mode, it makes learning more accessible.
Besides, I'd like to thank Jimmy for replying email so timely and answer my question so carefully! Next time you have a course with Jimmy as TA, don
t hesitate, just enroll in it.

sections.content:
This course covers some basic computer programming using Python, from loops to some basic of object-oriented programming. Also, this course uses a lot of Turtle Graphics (a kind of GUI).

This is not a difficult course if you have studied any programming language before, you just need to learn some syntax of Python. Even if you have never learnt any programming before, I still highly recommend you to study this course. You do not need to spend too much time to understand the code in the course. However, if you want to get a higher mark in this course, I suggest you to write some small program as practice each week to have a better understanding of the material taught in the course. You may also learn more about Python from other online material ( such as http://learnpython.org ) if you are really interested.

[General Course Schedule]
Week 1: Introduction to Python and Turtle Graphics
Week 2: If, then, else & Loops
Week 3: For loops
Week 4: Lists and Tuples
Week 5: Functions
Week 6: Stacks & Slice Notation
Week 7: Midterm
Week 8: Data Types Handling
Week 9: Turtle Window Events
Week 10: Dictionaries & Timers & Turtle Screen Event
Week 11: More on Operators & Colors & File Handling
Week 12 & 13: Object & Recursion

[Assignment 1 & 2]
Assignment 1 is to write a program that create a "L-system", while the second one is to create a Tetris Game.

If you follow the lab material well, you can complete 80-90% of the assignment. The remaining parts need to be programmed on your own.

[Midterm]
Midterm examination is a open book / open notes exam, but you cannot use a calculator during the exam. You can bring as much notes as you like, or even print out some code you wrote before. However, it does not help you much as the exam is mostly testing your logical thinking.

The exam may have some tricky part, such as:
- Data type (ex: integer and floating point)
- Functions (ex: global variable and local variable)

Therefore, be very careful when doing the midterm exam and try to avoid making any mistake. It is possible to attain full mark in the exam.

[Online Assignment]
This part is a special arrangement for this semester. I believe the coming semesters will use the original arrangement.

In the online assignment, there are more tricky questions than those in the midterm. For example, only part of the program is given and some content in the variable is hidden. However, you will have sufficient time to complete this assignment. You can try think of different case and run them on your computer. It is not that difficult if you can work with a computer rather than pen and paper only.

1. don't buy and bring the book to the mid-term / exam, totally useless. Because the test is examining your logic, not syntax. The book doesn't teach you logic. You will waste lots of time in reading book during test.

sections.content:
The course covers most of the fundamental concepts and logic in programming using the Python language and follows the textbook Interactive Python Programming For Beginners by Prof. Rossiter and Prof. Lam. Topics covered include:

1. Basic turtle graphics
2. For loops, while loops
3. Lists, tuples, strings and dictionaries
4. Defining functions
5. Window screen events
6. Basis in object-oriented programming
7. Recursion
sections.teaching:
The teaching was great. Prof. Rossiter's lectures were interesting and fun. He frequently asked questions in class so that you can get more practice in reading and understanding programs and codes. This certainly helped to consolidate materials taught in the lectures.

There are two TAs responsible for each lab session. They will guide you to complete the lab project step-by-step. However, you may skip all lab sessions if you think you can complete them on your own.
sections.grading:
There are 2 scoring schemes in this course:

Scheme A: Midterm 25% + Lab projects 32% + Final exam 43%

Scheme B: Midterm 0% + Lab projects 42% + Final exam 58%

The scheme that gives a higher overall score will be used to determine the final grade.

Given that I have almost no experience in programming, I got an A in this course. In my opinion, the course grading is excellent. It is quite easy to score full mark in lab projects as they are really simple, and the lab TA will show you almost all the codes you need for your lab project.

Midterm and final are easy (compared to other courses I have taken) but just quite tricky. Getting 80% or above is not hard if you are careful enough. Both midterm and final are open book, so they really test on your understanding of the logic of the programs.
sections.workload:
The workload is very light.

There is a lab project every week but only the odd-numbered ones are graded. In other words, there are altogether 8 lab projects in which 4 are graded. The lab projects are not hard at all and can be completed in less than 2 hours.

Since the midterm and final exams are both open-book, there is no need for any memorization. It is recommended that you should try understanding the logic of different codes through lab projects, or even try to design and write a program of some simple games. By doing so, studying for this course will be much fun.

sections.teaching:
Alex, the lecture instructor, would spend 80% of the lecture reading through the slides for the lectures before, and the rest 20% reading the ones for this lecture. The lecture time would be halved if he stops asking 'OK' after every piece of explanation.
Luke, the lab coach, would make some bugs due to typos, and he can't realize that. The lab time can also be halved if he use correction tools like grammarly or what so ever.
Though these instructors are nice guys, the documents can all be found online, and in most time they are just showing you through, so I cannot say this is high-quality teaching.
sections.grading: Grading is fine. But never hold the illusion that you can gain the bonus points. Though Alex claims that he picks people randomly, he actually has some preferred seats (I'd say he's never realized that). And every time a bonus question is raised, more than half of the class would raise their hands, but only one single student is lucky enough to be the chosen one.

sections.content:
No attendance requirement (Though bonus points are given in class, which counts toward your final score). I only attended 3 lectures.

The syllabus is fair. Gives you a general impression of what programming feels like. Not so helpful if you have a little programming experience. If you want more challenge, go get COMP1021P or take the C language waiver to start from COMP2011.

Only two assignments, each lasts about two weeks. It wouldn't be too hard if you put time into it even if you're just a beginner. Very detailed program structure was given to students so you can count on that if you need help. Most people were able to get full marks on their assignments.
sections.teaching:
Gibson is helpful (if you ask him questions within the syllabus. You won't be able to get specific python instructions on your own project.) and kind, and humorous, and cute.

Tutorial sucks. Just don't go. You'll be able to figure it out on your own before the instructor makes his way out of those bugs he writes.
sections.grading:
You might be able to outperform those students with more programming experience than you.
I strongly suggest that you don't rely on your very helpful docs and IDE all the time, as you would get a hard time eye-balling all bugs when you're in the exam. If you write your code with pretty good style, chances are that you'll be mad about those silly mistakes on the test paper that no human could ever make.
*For this term, the grading policy changed slightly. Mid-term will be considered 10% or 30% in your final score, so you won't be able to skip it and just get a full mark in your final.
sections.workload:
Very little workload if you get yourself a good IDE and enjoy typing, as most assignments are labor work and typist training.

However, you would like to get very familiar with the python module used in class (for this term, the turtle module). This saves you A LOT of time in your final to give you A LOT more time to debug and check your answers rather than referring to your cheatsheet all the time.

sections.content: Content was really fun, even though the nature of programming is supposed to be technical, we make games and animation. Not boring at all, attended 100% of the class. But then again, the basics are all the same, so learning this, you get the idea of how things run.
sections.teaching: David is really cool, he sounds very sarcastic but in a funny way. Learning environment was great, and engaging. Class atmosphere was fun, and i could tell that people are actually enjoying the class. There's tons of methods to get to an answer, but he always challenges the class how to cut the lines even shorter, which i thought was really an elegant way of writing codes.

Quiz and Exam is a bit tricky, because you gotta visualize the outcome just by looking at the code. For example, if you read this code, do you think the program will execute the desired outcome? or Fill in the blanks to make the code work. In the exam i just gave up on 2 questions because i was tired to think. Still got "A-". The mean of the class is about 70/100 at that time

sections.content: To be honest, this is the part which I personally as a student who have some background in programming have a mixed feeling about. The content itself is interesting, really, but you will only enjoy the content as much as I do if you do not struggle with the it. I can see that some really effort must have been put into selecting those interesting interactive examples which demonstrates what you can do by coding, but as far as I can tell, some of them are too complicated for new programmers to understand. Just like the final assignment a 500+LOC simple game which requires some serious planning job is just too much for some new learners to do on their own
sections.teaching: Gibson is really a very passionate instructor, which made the experience of this course really pleasant. I will not comment on how efficient the content was delivered during the course since I basically learned the python needed for the course just after an long afternoon in the library when I get the textbook, but if you have to take the course, I personally recommend Gibson over all other instructors.
sections.grading: Grading is fine. For the 2018-2019 fall semester, there is only 2 programming assignments and two exams, as long as you can use python and pay very close attention to the details of the requirements, you will do fine.
sections.workload: Fine for students who can write simple programming without much struggling, no matter if you have relative background knowledge or you are a really good learner (actually much lighter than MATH if you falls in this cat). Otherwise it might be a nightmare, since you might easily spend hours on some errors and have no progress at all.

sections.content: Very basic knowledge and concepts on Python programming. Focused a lot on the turtle graphics package. The Python language itself is easy to interpret, so this course is comparatively easier than COMP1022P and COMP1022Q.
sections.teaching: Give nice and very detailed explanation of course content. Good sense of humor and enjoys teaching the class. It makes it very easy to catch up (In case you missed lectures, or if you are not as good) though.
sections.grading: Not harsh, not difficult to reach A range but course mean is generally high. Exams however contains some tricky questions so make sure you revise your stuff thoroughly before taking it.
sections.workload: Low workload. The lectures and labs aren't compulsory, as long as you know your stuff. The two assignments requires more work and you may find some labs useful for it, so don't skip all of them. sections.content:
For a beginners programming python course, the course covers a lot of content. (ex. class and recursion)

No required textbook, but I would say the textbook is really helpful for beginners. Many of the examples are covered in the lectures, and there are exercise questions for you to try. The course will cover all the content in the textbook.

CH 1 : Introduction to Python
CH 2 : Basic Turtle Graphics Programming
CH 3 : Comments, Variables and Text
CH 4 : Variable Types and Operators
CH 5 : Making Decisions
CH 6 : Looping
CH 7 : Finding Repeating Patterns
CH 8 : Lists, Tuples and Strings
CH 9 : Functions
CH 10 : Dictionaries
CH 11 : More on Turtle
CH 12 : Turtle Window Event Handling
CH 13 : File Handling
CH 14 : Programming with Objects
CH 15 : Recursion

Personally, the content in the last 2 chapters were the most challenging
sections.teaching:
The professor is very approachable and willing to answer any and all questions that students have at the end of class. Although the class pace may seem to be fast at first (since he speaks very fast), he will do lots of revision at the start of each class which helps you remind the concepts and content learned in the previous lecture.

The lectures are recorded, so eve if you miss a lecture, you can still watch it later.
sections.grading:
Grading seems to be reasonable. Even if you don't do well not the mid-term, the professors will balance it so that the final weights more toward your grade (and vice-versa). However, there are many students in the course with prior experience in programming that will make very few mistakes in the exams, hence the s.d. is really high.

Mid-term (10%/25%): mean = 76.2/100, s.d. = 20.6

Final Examinations (60%/45%) : mean = 64/100, s.d. = 24.6

Assignment 1 (15%): mean = 90.5, s.d. = 25.9, max = 100, min = 5

Assignment 2 (15%): mean = 92.0, s.d. = 27.2, max = 100, min = 10
sections.workload:
The workload is average, only 2 mandatory assignments, but it is recommended to go through the examples in the lecture slides.

Many people say that the course has light workload, but if you have not done a lot of programming before (like me), the 2 assignments can take up a lot of time - especially the second assignment (creating a Pacman Game)

The professors frequently asks some questions based on lecture content that can earn you bonus marks. Just review the lecture slides, and this should be ok.

Two lectures and one lab per week.

Each lab is about 110 minutes, I was unfortunately enrolled in the 9:00am to 10:50pm session. There would be exactly one topic for every lab session. Sometimes the content could be taught a little earlier than the lectures, but for most of the time, what you see in labs have been taught before.

Very basic things about Python. In the last two lectures, Rossiter mentioned Objects and Recursion, I suppose these are for the 201X series?

sections.content:
Content is good for an introduction to programming and covers all of the basic concepts.

Content consists almost entirely of a series of PowerPoints (which happen to be available on the course website so lecture attendance is unnecessary). For those with any programming background at all, looking through the slides every so often is good enough to completely understand the course content.

Some of the concepts and techniques needed for completion of the assignments are introduced during the labs, but these materials are also available online and very easy to follow.
sections.teaching:
Lectures: Teaching is very slow (perhaps understandably so) and doesn't stray far from the PowerPoint slides. (I personally gave up on attending lectures after a week or two).

Labs: Better.
sections.grading:
Someone else will have posted the exact weightings (I don't remember them) but the main thing to note here is that your midterm grade is ignored and your final grade's weighting increased appropriately if your final grade would benefit from this. This means if the exam style catches you off guard during the midterm, you can remedy it for the final and it'll be as if it never happened.

Some of the exam questions give you part of a program and several blanks and ask you to fill them in to get a certain output. The questions in general are not difficult per se but can be tricky, so it's worth looking closely and thinking carefully about them and checking your steps if you have time at the end.

As for the two assignments: their weighting is significant and most people do very well, so make sure to follow the markscheme/spec very closely.
sections.workload: The only thing you have to do is two assignments, and these won't take very long at all if you've been following with the labs (which basically take you halfway through each already) and are familiar with the concepts introduced during lectures and labs. Going over the PowerPoints before the midterm and the final should be enough for preparation.

sections.grading:
Grading:
Mid-term:20%
Final:40%
Assignment: 40% (2 * 20%)

Or

Final 60%
Assignment: 40% (2 * 20%)
(if you mid-term exam will lower your grade)

My Score:
Mid-term: 82/100
Final: 92/100
Assignment 1: 100/100
Assignment 2: 100/100
Total: 95.2/100 (using second grading method)
Grade: A+

The exams and assignment are not difficult (except final exam, which is considerably harder than mid-term exam). You just need to take some time to work on them. Also, both exam is open book, so there shouldn't be much trouble on the exam. There will also be a set of revision notes provided before final exam(can be brought into final exam of course) so you can put all your effort in the final exam even if you failed in the mid-term exam.

But since this course is quite an easy course, the mean is also very high. You will need a high mark to get into A-range (~>90). Getting full marks on assignments are essential since they are quite easy. There will also be lab sections where you just work on the assignment, you ask the TA for help when you face any problems or difficulties.

The lecturer will also ask questions during lessons. If you answer them correctly (which, you should because the lecturer will help you even if you aren't quite sure about the answer), you will get some extra mark that will contribute to your assignment marks. (You can't get higher than full marks, this is only useful if you can't get full marks in the assignment)

sections.content:
Basic programming based on Python version 3.6
Content includes: (NOT in time order!)
1. Preparation (register for CSD account, set up Python, etc.)
2. Basic “Grammar” i.e. Syntax you should follow
3. Usage of Python turtle graphics (Basic drawing commands, EVENT HANDLING)
3. Loops (For, While)
4. Collections of data (list, tuple, dictionary)
5. Handling of those “collections” (access by index, slice notation, add/remove/reverse, etc.)
6. Data types and conversion (integer, float, string, etc.)
7. File handling (Read, Write, FORMATTED OUTPUT)
  7.1 String handling (Strip, Slice)
8. Functions (Creating, Calling w/ arguments)
  8.1 Global/Local variables
  8.2 Special: Event handling functions for turtle graphics
9. Basic Classes (Aka. Object-oriented programming) (Creating instance, interaction)
10. Basic Recursion (Recursion depth, judge what a recursion can do)

Note: No MIDI related stuff.
sections.teaching:
No attendance.

Gibson is a great instructor. Lectures are always fun and you can learn a lot. Never miss lectures.

He is helpful and willing to answer questions after lecture, in either English or Cantonese (But not Putonghua sorry...)

Labs are basically programming exercise, since I rarely attend them I can’t say much.

Lecture notes and Lab notes will be provided, no lecture video. But rarely will lectures teach something out of the note, so as the lab. Even in assignment labs (labs to give you some tips and help you finish the assignment), all the code provided in the lab will be in the note too, so don’t worry much if you skip it (Though I do NOT advise you to do so, since you can’t be sure to understand everything by just looking at the notes)

sections.content:
Note that the contents of this course vary from year to year, or maybe from semester to semester.

Python part:
1. Text input and output / Variables
2. if-else statements / nested-if
3. while loops / for loops / nested loops
4. Data structure: List and Tuples
5. Lindenmayer System (L-system)
6. Data structure: Stack
7. Functions
8. Operators and Data types
9. Data structure: Dictionary
10. File Handling
11. Objects
12. Recursion

Turtle Graphics part:
1. Moving and Drawing commands (turtle.up, turtle.forward, turtle.left, turtle.circle, etc.)
2. Commands to handle colours (turtle.color, turtle.colormode, etc.)
3. Filling commands (turtle.begin_fill, turtle.end_fill)
4. Text Input and Output commands (turtle.write, turtle.textinput, etc.)
5. Commands to control visibility (turtle.hideturtle.etc.)
6. Commands to control shape (turtle.shape, turtle.addshape, etc.)
7. Commands to control screen update (turtle.tracer, turtle.update)
8. Window setup command (turtle.mode, turtle.setup, etc.)
9. Event handling commands (turtle.onclick, turtle.ontimer, etc.)
10. Others (turtle.width, turtle.speed, turtle.Turtle, etc.)

The contents are quite easy, as long as you are willing to go through all the given notes thoroughly. Unlike COMP 1022P or Q, this course puts some stress on introducing the basics of computer science in line with teaching you to program in Python.
sections.teaching:
LAM, Gibson:
1. Easy-to-understand
2. Teaching (Speaking) style is generally funny

LAM, Ngok:
1. Very detailed explanation (sometimes lengthy though)
2. Boring (Sorry to say that, but it really is)

LAB (Ronald Mo):
easy-to-follow

Both lectures and labs don't take attendance. Generally all three of them are okay. Just sit whoever you like and ask whatever you want to (they are willing to answer any questions).
sections.grading:
Grading is based on
1. Two assignments (total 40%, 20% each)
2. Midterm (20%)
3. Final (40%)

Assignments:
The two assignments of this semester are both a bit tricky, but you can still figure it out by devoting a little bit of your time. In general, they are easy-to-handle. Getting full marks is a must.

However, you should be reminded that you better finish the assignments ON YOUR OWN, and make sure that your work is not accidentally LEAKED. You will certainly score zero in assignment if professors find any trace of copying (from your work or in your work), and no matter what your reason/excuse is, professors will regard you as plagiarizing.

Midterm:
Tricky and demanding in speed. In this semester we have only 1 hour to finish the paper, and comparatively the paper is not really short.

Final:
Tricky and difficult. For some questions what I can really do is pure guessing.

Generally, the use of various data structures (lists, tuples, dictionary) with looping and L-systems with recursion are the main points in this semester. Also, as stated in the title, easy contents do not guarantee you a good performance in exams or a satisfactory grade. But still, at least try your best to avoid careless mistakes !

Overall statistics for reference:
Assignment 1: max 100; min 5; avg 91.8; sd 18.1
Assignment 2: max 100; min 3; avg 90.9; sd 27.65
Midterm: max 100; min 18; avg 66.9; sd 21.8
Final: max 100, min 8; avg 53.9; sd 25.1
(Zeros are all excluded)

My result
Assignments: both 100/100
Midterm: 89/100
Final: 71/100
Overall: 86.2% (A-)

The grading is fair I guess. But an A- is a bit below my expectation. Thanks for the final !

But I advise spending more time on practicing to trace the code involving lists / tuples / dictionaries with loops (in particular nested-loops).

sections.content: Although the name suggests “Intro to CS”, it’s actually just basic programming in Python.
sections.teaching: Most of the time, content presented in the classroom is covered in the lecture notes. But sometimes the instructor will use other examples, which are more interesting than those in lecture notes. For example, he uses real midterm data (scores, student ID, lecture section) to teach us file reading in python. He knows the materials quite well, and he does try to make the lessons interesting. Sometimes he will ask questions, you get assignment points (used to boost assignments marks if you didn’t get full marks) for answering them correctly.
sections.grading:
Assignment 1 (20%)
Assignment 2 (20%)
Midterm (20%)
Final (40%)

This is the regular grading methodology, however if you didn’t perform well in the midterm, and you manage to do very well in the final, they automatically exclude your midterm score in the total grade. In this case, final will weigh 60% in the total grade. However take note that final is definitely more difficult than midterm.

Overall, the grading scheme is quite generous. 99% for assignment 1, 100% for assignment 2, 94% for midterm, 94% for final = A+ , but I guess I’m on the boundary between A and A+ since the high score is always 100, better be extremely careful and score full marks if you aim for A+.

Assignment 1 mean score : 89.9, SD : 15.43
Assignment 2 mean score : 94.1, SD : 12.67
Final mean score : 62.3, SD : 22.6
Midterm mean score : 69.1, SD : 22.2
sections.workload:
The workload for this course is acceptable, might be heavier for beginners in programming. If you are somehow new to any programming language, then simply reading the lecture notes might not be enough, if you want to secure good grade, practice coding from scratch or tweaking code presented in lecture notes can help you get familiar with the course materials. There’s lectures and lab every week, no attendance is taken though. Skipped two of the lectures, and two of the labs. You can self study lecture notes if you miss the lecture. For lab, the detailed instructions are posted on the lab website, so no worries if you accidentally skipped it. By the way, lab 3 and 4, 7 and 8 (I skipped these two) are related to the assignments. You will eventually use code written in lab to complete the assignments.

Code for assignment 1 (use turtle graphics and pygame midi module to implement a fairly simple “music player”) can be written in less than a day, since they really provide a lot of guidance in the assignment document. But be sure to spend (possibly a lot of) time to test the program!

Assignment 2 (use turtle graphics to implement a space shooter game) will take more time to complete. Searching for game materials to use, and editing them, might take as much time as writing the code. I spend a few days on assignment 2, possibly because I prefer working in a relaxed mode. Just don’t procrastinate and you will be fine for both assignments. You can always approach TA to seek help in completing assignments, they are very willing to help. But as the deadline gets closer, they might be very busy because many students need their help.

Midterm and final are open book and open notes examinations, so you will be fine provided that you are familiar with the materials, and understand the concepts.

sections.content: The course teaches simple python syntaxes and how computer logic works. sections.grading: Although the course is relatively easy, many students who have taken python prior to this course are also present, so it is hard to go from a B range to an A range. To get an A range grade overall, a perfect score on the assignment is a must. The final exam questions difficulty increases every semester, so it is important to master the past papers and take some supplementary python practice problems on your own.
sections.workload: Lecture notes are around 20 slides each. Each set took me about 20-30 minutes to review and learn on my own, so the lectures themselves are not too heavy at all. Assignments tend to take more time, because the smallest mistakes can cause a big problem in the program. You will suffer less if you just take it to the TA or a friend who had taken this course when these situations occur. Don't overwork your brain.. it will be hard to find those errors on your own.

sections.content:
This course teaches basic programming concepts through Python 2.0. These concepts include, but are not limited to, the following:
-> Variables
-> Functions
-> Classes
-> Recursion
-> Operators
-> For/While loops
-> Dictionaries, tuples and lists
-> Stacks
-> If/Nested-if statement

These concepts are mostly taught using the built-in turtle graphics to help visualise the aforementioned concepts.
sections.teaching: Prof. Gibson Lam is an enthusiastic instructor, and knows how to explain the materials to students with little to no programming background. He also thoroughly prepares for each lecture, as he always makes simple programs before the lecture to illustrate its contents more easily to students. He is also willing to help you if you have any questions regarding programming.
sections.grading:
There are two types of grading. One is where your mid-term exam's result is counted while the other is where that result is not counted. This depends on how well you did for your mid-term exam. If your final grade will be brought down as a result of your exam when compared to counting it out of the final grade calculation, then it will be omitted.

You can also get bonus points for your assignment by answering Prof. Gibson Lam's questions during the lecture. However, your total assignment grade cannot be brought above 44% total when including the bonus points.

Grading with mid-term exam result:
22% Assignment 1
22% Assignment 2
22% Mid-term Exam
34% Final Exam

Grading without mid-term exam result:
22% Assignment 1
22% Assignment 2
56% Final Exam

If your final grade is at the mean, plus or minus 1 SD, you will lie in the B-range. Getting 1 SD above mean will give you a grade lying in the A range.
sections.workload:
The two assignments given will have 80% of its contents covered during the lab sessions. In other words, the lab sessions are a great way to go through the assignments if you need assistance in them. Also, you are given a few weeks to complete the assignments, which should be ample time to get them done.

Both exams are 'open-note, open-book' exams, which means you can bring as many materials as you like to the exam as long as they are not electronic or smart devices. You may print out all the lecture slides and bring them to the lecture. A summary of all the contents covered will also be given just before each exam.

And then, well, I stopped going to class. So I don't really know what the classes were like after the second lecture.

Same goes for the labs (oops).
sections.grading:
22% Assignment 1
22% Assignment 2
34% Final
22% Optional Midterm (weight will be moved to the final)

Got mean, was a B.
sections.workload: Too light. Spent 10 hours overall studying and working on projects for the course. There should be more coding practice involved.

sections.content: The content of the course is quite good, the lecture slides are high quality and the assignments are enjoyable and not difficult. The language taught is Python, which is in my opinion the best language for beginners.
sections.teaching: Teaching is acceptable. The pace is quite slow especially if you know some programming, but is tolerable.
sections.grading:
Grading is very nice. Exams are not difficult, but sometimes tricky. Assignments are easy, the slides quite literally walk you through the whole assignment so you don't have to do anything but to implement what you're told.
The midterm mark is omitted if you end up with a higher overall grade without it. I did relatively bad on the midterm, but ended up with an A+ thanks to the final.
sections.workload: All the exams are open notes, so there's actually no need to study for them. There are two assignments that are easy and can be done entirely in a couple of hours.

sections.content: For any student who is being acquainted to programming for the first time, the course does look interesting. The programming language taught here is Python, which has a simpler syntax as compared to other languages like Java or C++. However, if you are looking at this course from the perspective of going for a major in Computer Science, I would recommend you to skip this course and instead look at COMP1022P.
sections.teaching: Professor Rossiter is a great professor, who is so lively that you seldom feel sleepy in his class. He has a great and a very understandable accent, and he knows how to engage the class.
sections.grading:
The marks distribution used is:
Midterm 22%
Assignment-1 22%
Assignment-2 22%
Final exam 34%
However, if using the midterm mark gives you a lower end-of-semester score, then your midterm mark will be automatically ignored. It will be worth 0 percent of the course to you. In this situation, the marks distribution used used would be:
Midterm 0%
Assignment-1 28.25%
Assignment-2 28.25%
Final exam 43.5%
So based on this, it is lenient to an acceptable level.
sections.workload: The course has lectures, tutorials and laboratories. So it does have a considerable amount of workload. But in general, the amount of time you need to spend on each topic is pretty low and the course content is very generic and basic.

sections.content:
Python 3.2, Topic大部份同中學ICT Programming一樣(唔贅述, 其他review寫得好好)
　
佢個網站會有齊所有野, lecture slides, example program, cheatsheet....
　
Python多左個叫Turtle既東西, 可以用黎畫下公仔既....
然後會用到其中一個額外library 'pygame', 除左assignment之外應該冇用, 考試都唔洗特別背code, 因為open notes....
sections.grading:
Assignment x2 @22%; Midterm 22%; Final 34%
Midterm冇考/考得差的話可以唔計, 呢個case既話Final 56%
平時落堂之前會問幾條問題, 答岩一題有1分加落assignment, 當你assignment唔高分果陣應該有用
　
mean/SD
assignments: 89.1/18, 92.7/15
midterm: 69.6/17 ; final: 69/23.2
所以assignment最好滿分
　
因為考試open notes, 所以自製/佢比既cheatsheet有code都要非常小心, final因為咁失左少少分, 其他滿分, A+
sections.workload:
輕鬆, lab係幫你做assignment, 正常冇壓力
如果冇上過堂, 最好assignment deadline前早d追返哂所有野+做assignment
　
assignment應該會定期改一次題目, 就算topic同上年一樣, 比分位都會唔同左, 有source都冇乜用

sections.content: The content is very fun and applicable. You get to build your own game. Good course for programming novices who want their first experience with a programming language.
sections.teaching: Rossiter is the better professor. He makes the class very interesting and definitely does not make it difficult to want to attend class.
sections.grading: Grading is okay. Just do relatively well and it should be at least a B+.
sections.workload: Workload is not too much. There are a few assignments but overall, the midterm and final do not require much studying at all.

sections.content: Learn about basic programming skills in 'Python' including "Hello World" and other terminologies with hands-on lab sessions on Functions, Arrays, Recursion, GUI and even a slight touch on Classes.
sections.teaching: David Rossiter is a FANTASTIC professor. Teaches the concepts in a really passionate way so that students can get the idea really easily and quickly. Greatest professor ever met in terms of teaching in UST.
sections.grading: A Common Core course with nice grading. Exams are very easy with those who have the necessary skillets for computer science.
sections.workload: Workload is alright. No group project for the best part (unlike many other common core courses). Assignments can be annoying and time consuming sometimes but it's really fun to do.

sections.content:
Basic Python programming.
For students who want a easier course may take the VBA course instead. But this course is not too diffiicult though.
sections.teaching:
David will demonstrate every examples showed on the notes so it is suggested to attend the lectures.

Attendance of lab sections is not required, but I highly suggest student not to miss any of the lab section because many of the assignment details will be go through during the lab.
sections.grading: Great. I think above mean a sd can get a A grade or so.
sections.workload:
The "game" assignment is interesting.
Exam is open-notes.

sections.content: Very BASIC programming concept. If...then...else, loops and etc.
sections.teaching: Very funny and energetic instructor, should not have any problem understanding his English.
sections.grading: As long as you do the programming assignments yourself without copying each other, you should not have any problem with your midterm and final. Students without programming background should be able to get B range or above. (As long as you are not terrible at programming)
sections.workload: The only workload is the programming assignment. It depends on whether you are terrible at understanding basic programming concept or not.

sections.content: The course is designed as a introductory, so it didn't cover many topics which are important for Python. A bit inadequate for people who wish to learn more about Python or CS students. Anyway, not bad.
sections.teaching: Rossiter is very funny. His lectures are always full of laughs. And obviously he is a native speaker.  He is also willing to answer students' questions.
sections.grading: Everyone I know got good grades, like A or A+. The projects are quite easy and if written appropriately. Even if someone scored poorly in the midterm, with a little effort, could get A or higher.
sections.workload: It's work on programming is too little as a CS course. Only a few hundreds of codes per project. And a student proficient in programming could finish that two hours.

sections.content:
教用Python寫program,都係d
-Type of variables
-while / for loop
-function
-if
-recursion
等等比較易上手既topic
sections.teaching:
一個好有趣既外藉professor,上堂唔悶,講野都幾易明,間中抽人答問題:)
不過好唔中意人嘈,傾計太大聲會比佢話:(
sections.grading: grade都唔錯,2份功課都幾高分,但final得mean,最後B左
sections.workload: workload唔太大,一個sem只係要交2份assignment,其他lab都唔計分。而兩份assignment上堂都會教你做大概1/3先,有上堂既話淨番既應會識做,就算唔識搵TA幫手佢地都好肯解答問題!!所以功課唔難高分;)

sections.content: 简单的Python，入门。如果没有基础又想学programming的话应该会喜欢这种课。
sections.teaching: 幽默，轻松。TA也都很负责，会解答问题，还有视频可以帮助复习。
sections.grading: 细心点，有好龟。但是题目简单大家分数都高了，基本不能有错，如果要A+
sections.workload: 基本为零。两次assignment。一次midterm，一次final。都是开卷考。

sections.content: 都是程序很基礎的知識，雖然不深，但對於後續的學習會蠻有用。
sections.teaching:
非常有趣，很難有困意。
add/drop period會把所有的slides都替我們印出來，很貼心的。
sections.grading: 給的grade算是很好的了，assignment和midterm final都不難。
sections.workload: 有兩個大assignment，沒有其他作業，課後只需把程序自己玩一遍即可。

sections.content: Contents are interesting and useful, especially if you are considering to learn more about programming. Even if you don't, you get to learn the logic people use in Computer Science, and it's quite useful, I guess.
sections.teaching: Rossiter was very organized, very structured and very helpful. He tried to make the class not to be boring. His ppts are very detailed and complete, I sometimes find this annoying because I can't jot notes in class because everything's there already, but I guess it's good if you're planning not to come to class at all. Lecture videos are also provided.
sections.grading: Gradings were alright. The midterm was too easy (the bell curve was not really a bell, it was left skewed) and most people got almost to full marks in the assignments, thus making competition to be really tight in the course.
sections.workload: Compared to other courses I have taken in UST, there are quite a lot of things you have to do for this course. Other than just studying, you need to practice (a lot) and finish 2 assignments. They're not really hard, but they still take up some time.

sections.content: Basic Python programming language. No need for computer background.
sections.teaching:
Excellent teacher

Very engaging and humorous to keep lectures fun and exciting. Explains everything step-by-step to make sure everyone even without computer background can understand.

Powerpoint notes are very straightforward and concise, uploaded online each week. Can ask questions after lectures or TAs in lab time, they are friendly and willing to help.
sections.grading: Reasonable grading, ~1SD for A range
sections.workload:
Low workload

Two assignments that can be mostly completed during lab time, a final and an optional midterm (both open-note).

Even if you cannot attend the lectures, they are filmed and uploaded online, no attendance required.

sections.content:
學programming入面嘅python（？）

學完之後會識得用佢嚟整啲小遊戲，都幾開心幾有成功感

會學到基本嘅programming語言
sections.teaching:
表示係ust聽咗咁多難聽嘅英文之後，聽rossiter嘅英文會令你】你覺得你進入咗第二個世界，絕對聽出耳油 ，佢把聲同迪士尼讀故仔嗰啲差唔多

由於呢個course係比啲未接觸過programming嘅人讀，所以佢每部分都會講得好明，加埋勁多example，務求令你明晒先落堂， 佢仲要成日搞爛gag同自嘲，唔會令你覺得悶

sections.content: 成個Course都係學python, 由基本syntax開始. for loop, if-else, while loop, recursion, object, etc..

sections.content:
The course format is basically two exams, 2-3 assignments, labs and an individual project.

The syllabus covers the basics of Python, loops, data types and the Turtle graphic library.

There is no attendance requirement for the lectures. Do attend the labs as you get to ask the TAs about your assignments/labs.
sections.teaching:
The lecturer always teaches with passion and presents material in humorous way.

The TAs are typically helpful with your work. Ask and you can receive.
sections.grading: The grading is reasonable. The exam format is MC plus short questions (code filling etc.)
sections.workload:
No reading or online homwork.
There are weekly labs and several assignments to be completed.

The assignments mostly involve completing skeleton codes etc.

sections.content: Teaching the basic concept of programming using Python. Python is a relatively easy programming language for beginners because the codes are like English. You have to attend most of the lessons in order to get familiar with the logic flows for exam.
sections.teaching: Really fun. The professor can give you a happy lesson. I Promise.
sections.grading: This course is easy. You may feel disappointed when you get B range even you achieve 90% or above. But, the grading is still reasonable.
sections.workload:
One midterm
Two assignments
One final exam

Actually, the workload is low. You can learn a lot from doing assignment. Remember do them by yourself, you will feel hopeless in final exam if your assignments are carried by your friends.

sections.content: How to use Python 2.3. While loop, for loop, if conditions, hello world, pygame, turtle graphics etc.
sections.teaching:
Fun. At least not boring
The lab sessions are useful for homework and you can try what you have learnt in lectures by making some games
sections.grading:
Quite Good. Mean = B
Getting full marks in assignments is quite easy because you can keep making corrections before the due date of the homework.
sections.workload:
Few.Only 2 assignments which 60% of content will be taught during lessons. 40% have to complete by yourself.
Exams are open booked. You just need to revise a little bit at home before examinations

sections.content: Basic Python Programming. For example, variable declaration, for/while loop, if-then-else statement. Clear Notes.
sections.teaching: Actually I didn't attended all the lessons, but David is good at teach us thinking step by step. Overall I would highly recommend him.
sections.grading: Very Good, you can earn A range for above mean 1 SD,  and A+ for above mean 1.5 SD.
sections.workload:
Very Little.
Only 2 Assignment for writing a music player and a simple game. No attendance is taken so that you can simply refer to the video taken which is available on the course portal.

sections.content: Basic python skills. For those without any computer background, it is also easy to understand.
sections.teaching: It is good to attend David's lecture. You will never feel boring in the lesson.
sections.grading: normal grading. I got mean in the final exam but below one SD in the midterm exam. I got a B in the result.
sections.workload: With the help of TA, it is quite easy to finish the assignment . Actually, you can finish most part of the assignment in computer labs, we just need to add a few at home.

sections.content:
呢個Course 係programming嘅入門班，如果之前有讀過ICT programming會好快上手。個course主要教你用python去學習programming嘅basic idea，同埋會學一d python特有嘅syntax，再會教你用d python好容易做到嘅function例如turtle同埋music playing。

連考法都好似ICT programming咁，比blank你填code，dry run code等等。
sections.teaching:
都冇咩上lecture其實lol，不過感覺上Gibson都講得幾清晰。反而我有去足lab，個TA（好似叫Catherine）教得好好，同埋問佢問題佢都用心解答，所以強烈推薦上lab，因為我覺得lab做嘅野等於課堂內容精華版，落手做好快吸收。

雖然我係學過C 所以覺得有d syntax唔洗解釋咁多，不過我覺得d lecture notes真係有d類聚，因為我自己整咗個份神notes入去考都係得5頁就有齊成個course嘅內容，不過呢個course連final前派嘅cheatsheet都有幾多頁下...
sections.grading: 我覺得OK好grade啦，我兩份assignment都滿分，midterm 高個幾sd, final高一個sd，最後有A，不過真係feel唔到點先會有A＋lol
sections.workload: 唔算太重，有兩份assignment，lab唔計attendance又冇野交，基本上靜係教你做assignment個幾個 lab先去上都ok。final理論上唔會考翻midterm前嘅內容，只不過讀親programming點都要承繼翻basic嘅idea同syntax咁姐。

sections.content:
Language: Python

內容不要期待太多，正如普通的入門programming course一樣，教的是
loop
drawing
if statement
array indexing
import/save file 之類的東西

Tips: 請注意每個command的用法，是用法。注意哪些指令會call variable。多想像些奇怪的situation,考試就是考這些。

ps: physics同學，python 遲些有用
sections.teaching:
首先請認實DAVID ROSSITER !
英國人，上堂風趣幽默，喜歡自嘲，九點堂都很難有睡意。英語清晰，條理算是分明。

隨堂派note,final前派cheatsheet,那份cheatsheet叫一個歎為觀止，從每一個command的用途，用法到例子應有盡有，本來自己寫了cheatsheet都不想用了。
sections.grading:
grade神
1. 高一個sd就有A (我那年80%)
2. 考試每一題都很重要，錯一條基本一個sub-grade(當年我有個中同mid-term多錯一條就 A-了。。）
sections.workload:
2 assignments+midterm+final+Lab(?)

Labs：
Lab不take attendance。
去了基本浪費時間，TA基本把可以20分鐘打完的code說整堂。
但...是...
lab的material很重要，請自己做，自己做。

assignment 2:

(如果不肯定就拿去給TA看，有時候TA會順手幫你做完）

注意：Assignment請拿滿分

Exams:
cheatsheet allowed
MC/fill in the blanks questions

sections.content: 讀CS既入門course，用python，比C, C++容易，如果有讀過ICT唔會好難。除左Command line既program外，仲會學graphic同music的
sections.teaching: David教得幾好幾清晰，上佢堂唔會悶，佢幾搞笑
sections.grading: 好grade，我第一份assignment做左一半就交左，第二份有做晒，midterm, final above mean，最後有A
sections.workload: 唔算重，兩份assignment，midterm，final，每星期都有lab但唔計attendance而且冇野交，如果冇野問自己係屋企做都得

sections.content:
呢個Course 係programming 的入門班，主要教你少少programming 的idea 同埋基本的 syntex (if ... then ..., function, class etc.)，主要考你logic。學完之後要寫一d 用黎計數的 program 絕對無問題，但如果要識用到同system 有關的野，就要再take d 深d 的course。

每星期會有Lab，主要係實戰，唔計attendance，不過都建議上，有咩唔識可以搵TA carry 下。
sections.teaching:
Prof. 係英國佬，英文好聽，上堂成日搞下gag ，抽下水，絕無冷場，表達能力幾好，聽完多數都明。

Notes 黎講算唔差，但都建議上堂，如果唔係都有機會唔知notes up 乜。

Tutorial TA 會帶你寫一個小型program，等你熟習上堂學過的野，會慢慢比時間你試，都幾nice。
sections.grading:
考試多數Short Q 或者 MC，total 得20條左右，睇落好易，但極多trap，一唔小心就無5%。另外雖然係Open notes，但都建議背定入去，因為到時都幾chur 下，未必有時間睇。

Final 會易過mid term 同時間多好多，可以cover mid term。另外有兩份assigment，主要base on tutorial 教過的野再加dd function，要滿分唔難，建議同人交換個program 玩下先交。

筆者overall 90%，A。
sections.workload: 主要都係上下堂同tutorial，assignment 最好自己做，否則final 好易GG。考之前狂睇example 同背下code，開個Python 練習下，到時冷靜d 高分唔難。

sections.content: After all, the content of the course is easy, especially for those with little programming background and took ICT as an elective for HKDSE. What was being taught in the course is just introductory programming like FOR and WHILE loop. If you are with programming background and careful enough, this course will be a piece of cake for you.
sections.teaching: Dr Rossiter is quite a good lecturer as he was able to give lecture with great intonation (in the mean that you won't speak in that way in daily life). With his funny and some anti-logical example, the atmosphere in the class is not boring at all.
sections.grading: You don't have to be panic if you didn't make a good trial in midterm, your midterm result will be eliminated if it lower your overall score in the ordinary scheme (scheme 1 is accounting all your results from assignments, midterms and final; scheme 2 is accounting only your assignments and finals). To conclude, what is important is carefulness.
sections.workload: There are only two assignments in the entire semester. Programming a music player and a game. Again, if you are careful enough, it is not difficult to score a full mark in both assignments.

如果有上堂係會識嘅
